1.explanation:
• comparison.md contains Prettier’s existing comparisons between parsers and performance numbers, matching the screenshot table format.  
• technical-details.md explains the integration points and architecture of the parser in Prettier, critical to swapping parsers.  
• rationale.md outlines the motivations and trade-offs of using a particular parser (why Babylon was chosen).  
• related-projects.md lists alternative parsers (including Cherow) and points to their feature matrix, which is necessary to evaluate support gaps (e.g. Flow support).
1.bug_scenario: The user is reporting that Prettier’s current JavaScript parser (Babylon) is too slow for format-on-save workflows and suggests switching to the Cherow parser, which benchmarks about 40% faster. The attached screenshot is a table of parse times (in ms) across several popular codebases (jQuery, Angular, React, TypeScript, etc.) for multiple parsers (Cherow, Esprima, Acorn, Espree, Shift, Babylon). The scenario involves understanding how parser speed impacts overall formatting performance, and the blocker is that Cherow doesn’t yet support Flow syntax.
